legend: The cartilage component of the tumour and a mesenchymal component made of undifferentiated small round or spindled cells are seen.

T1-weighted postcontrast fat saturation MRI shows a left orbital conus mass. The two components are subtle with mostly a solid enhancing (round cell component) appearance with subtle flecks of heterogeneous density (cartilage component).

A different case of orbital mesenchymal chondrosarcoma to the one shown in <<33858>>, with the same transition from a round cell component to a cartilage component, with resting chondrocytes at the interface.
A case of orbital mesenchymal chondrosarcoma with transition from a round cell component to a cartilage component, with resting chondrocytes at the interface.

A round cell to matrix transition with the matrix exhibiting a zonal endochondral ossification-like progression of cartilage to bone/mineralization is seen. At the interface between the round cells and cartilage on the lower right are resting, then proliferative, then hypertrophic chondrocytes, with ossification/mineralization at the upper left.
This master regulator of chondrogenesis, SOX9, stains in both round cells and cartilage, indicating that the primitive round cell component is composed of immature cartilage-phenotype cells.
